triggers.cause_object_ref: input_text: Distinguish implementation consequence from abstraction in this design.
triggers.phase_relevance: Addresses the boundary between what is necessarily a result of implementation details and what is defined at the abstraction level in the design.
triggers.materiality_reason: A responsible distinction between implementation-level consequences and abstract properties is required before analysis; requested operation is meaningful only if this distinction is feasible in the input.
triggers.admitting_rule: Structural cause, gap flagged as meaningful for operation-projection (operation applies if input supports a non-coerced distinction).

projection_synthesis_proposal.ontology_hypothesis: Design-level objects can be decomposed into abstract properties (specified in the design independently of implementation) and implementation consequences (effects or features that arise solely due to particular implementation choices).
recognition_criteria: An implementation consequence is an effect, feature, or property of the design that arises only from the chosen implementation and would not necessarily be true in all valid realizations of the abstraction.
An abstraction-level property is any constraint, goal, or specification present in the design regardless of implementation.
projection_synthesis_proposal.segmentation_policy_hint: Partition analysis into two: what must be true in all conforming implementations (abstraction) and what may be true in just this implementation (consequences).
evidence_requirements: Clear description or specification of both abstraction constraints and implementation details.
Ability to trace design properties to either high-level specification or implementation artifact.
exclusions: Features simultaneously required by the abstraction and implementation are not exclusively classified as implementation consequences.
contraindications: Insufficient information about either the abstraction or the implementation prevents a reliable distinction.
applicability_assumptions: Input provides distinguishable information about abstraction versus implementation.
